title: Dense affine shrinking makes the boundary of a relative affine line finite
statement: Let Y be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] with coordinate ring finite type over the integers, and let U be a dense open of its relative affine line [def-nagata-relative-affine-space]. There exist a commutative ring R finite type over the integers, an open immersion g:Spec R→Y with dense image, and a closed immersion i:Z→A¹_(Spec R) whose image is the complement of the inverse image of U, such that the composite Z→Spec R is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

proof.text: Finite type over the integers makes Y and its relative line Noetherian. The projection is open, continuous and surjective, so the image of U is dense open. A dense open contains every component generic point: isolate its component from the other finitely many components and use density, then specialization.

Each generic fibre is an irreducible affine line over a residue field and meets U. Its nonempty open has finite complement by the dimension-one bound; injectivity of the closed immersion gives finite generic fibres for the boundary.
Apply the generic-finiteness neighborhood theorem to the reduced closed complement of U, obtaining a dense open V of Y where that complement is finite.

In Spec Γ(Y,top), finite prime avoidance finds an element of the vanishing ideal of the complement of V avoiding every minimal prime. Its principal open W is contained in V and dense. Its coordinate ring remains finite type over the integers. Identify W with its affine spectrum and pull back the original closed complement using the affine-space cartesian square; finiteness follows by base change. Empty and nonreduced schemes are included.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_dense_affine_open_isFinite_closedComplement
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] [Algebra.FiniteType ℤ Γ(Y, ⊤)]
    (U : (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) Y).Opens)
    (hU : Dense (U : Set (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) Y))) :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : Algebra.FiniteType ℤ R)
      (g : Spec (.of R) ⟶ Y) (_ : IsOpenImmersion g),
      Dense (Set.range g.base) ∧
      ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) (Spec (.of R)))
        (_ : IsClosedImmersion i),
        Set.range i.base =
          ((AffineSpace.map (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) g ⁻¹ᵁ U :
            (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) (Spec (.of R))).Opens) : Set _)ᶜ ∧
        IsFinite (i ≫
          (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) (Spec (.of R)) ↘ Spec (.of R)))

mathlib_searches.query: Dense open in an affine finite-type integer scheme contains a dense principal open; a relative affine line dense-open complement is generically finite
mathlib_searches.results: Read returned signatures: affineOpens, affineBasicOpen, dense affine Zariski subsite, PartialMap.Opens.isDominant_ι, isCompact_and_isOpen_iff_finite_and_eq_biUnion_basicOpen. None states the needed shrinking theorem.

mathlib_searches.query: A dense open of a relative affine line has finite complement after shrinking to a dense affine open of the Noetherian affine base
mathlib_searches.results: Returned signatures concern basicOpen constructibility, affine Zariski cover density and equality of restricted sections. No compact-support or shrinking match.

Read Mathlib prime avoidance and minimal-prime topology, and source AffineSpace.Fiber, ConstructibleSheaf.GenericConstancy and Mathlib.Topology.KrullDimension. Reused the dimension-one finite-boundary theorem and generic constancy; no duplicate of these three new statements.
